# R Programming Reference Guide

## Methods & Functions Reference

### Basic Operations
| Function | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `c()` | Combine values into a vector |
| `seq()` | Generate sequences (`by`, `length.out`) |
| `rep()` | Repeat elements |
| `1:10` | Shortcut for `seq(1,10)` |
| `rnorm()` | Random normal distribution |
| `runif()` | Random uniform distribution |
| `rpois()` | Random Poisson distribution |
| `log()`, `sin()`, `cos()` | Math functions |
| `mean()`, `sum()`, `sd()` | Statistics |
| `length()`, `dim()`, `nrow()`, `ncol()` | Get dimensions |
| `ls()` | List objects in environment |
| `rm(list=ls())` | Clear environment |

### Data Structures
| Function | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `matrix()` | Create matrix (`nrow`, `byrow`) |
| `cbind()`, `rbind()` | Bind columns/rows |
| `data.frame()` | Create data frame |
| `list()` | Create list |
| `as.matrix()`, `as.data.frame()` | Convert types |
| `as.factor()` | Convert to categorical |
| `rownames()`, `colnames()` | Get/set names |
| `diag()` | Diagonal matrix |

### Accessing Elements
| Operator | Usage |
|----------|-------|
| `[ ]` | Vectors/matrices: `x[3]`, `A[2,3]`, `A[1:2,4:5]` |
| `[[ ]]` | List by index: `L[[3]]` |
| `$` | List by name: `L$v3` |
| `-` | Exclude: `x[-3]`, `x[-c(1,3,5)]` |

### Missing Values
| Function | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `NA` | Missing value marker |
| `is.na()` | Detect missing values |
| `na.rm=TRUE` | Ignore NA in calculations |

---

## Data Types

| Type | Example | Note |
|------|---------|------|
| Numeric | `2.5`, `-3.14` | Default number type |
| Integer | `1L`, `2L` | Explicit with `L` suffix |
| Boolean | `TRUE`, `FALSE` | Avoid `T`/`F` shortcuts |
| Character | `"hello"`, `'a'` | Strings |
| Factor | `as.factor(c("M","F"))` | Categorical variables |
| Vector | `c(1,2,3)` | 1D, same type only |
| Matrix | `matrix(1:6, nrow=2)` | 2D, same type only |
| Data Frame | `data.frame(...)` | 2D, mixed types per column |
| List | `list(...)` | Mixed types and sizes |

> ⚠️ Don't mix types in vectors/matrices - R will coerce to single type!

---

## Programming Constructs

### For Loop
```r
for (i in 1:10) { print(i) }
for (i in c('a','b','c')) print(i)  # No braces if single line
```

### While Loop
```r
x = 10
while (x > 0) { print(x); x = x - 1 }
```

### If/Else
```r
if (condition) {
  # code
} else {
  # code
}
if (cond) action1 else action2  # Single line
```

### Switch
```r
switch(exp, "sin" = sin(x), "cos" = cos(x))
```

### Break & Warning
```r
for (i in l) {
  if (i < 0) { warning("Negative!"); break }
}
```

---

## Defining Functions

```r
myfunction <- function(param1, param2 = default_value, ...) {
  # ... passes extra args to subfunctions like plot()
  result = param1 + param2
  return(result)
}
```

> **Key points:**
> - Variables inside functions are local
> - Global variables are visible inside functions (be careful!)
> - Use `package::function()` to access masked functions (e.g., `base::sum()`)

---

## Plot Types (Base R)

| Type | Code | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| Points | `type='p'` | Scatter plot (default) |
| Lines | `type='l'` | Line plot |
| Both | `type='b'` | Points + lines |
| Histogram-like | `type='h'` | Vertical lines |
| Stairs | `type='s'` | Step function |
| Nothing | `type='n'` | Empty plot (useful for layering) |

### Plot Customization
```r
plot(x, y, xlab="X", ylab="Y", main="Title", 
     col="blue", pch=19, lty=2, lwd=2,
     col.main="lightblue")
lines(x, z, col="red", lty=2)  # Add line to existing plot
hist(x, breaks=30, col="#007bc2", freq=FALSE)
lines(density(x), col="red")   # Add density curve
```

## ggplot2

### Basic Structure
```r
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data = df) +
  geom_*(aes(x = var1, y = var2, color = var3, fill = var4)) +
  theme_light()
```

### Geom Types
| Geom | Usage |
|------|-------|
| `geom_point()` | Scatter plot |
| `geom_line()` | Line plot |
| `geom_smooth()` | Trend line (`method='loess'`) |
| `geom_histogram()` | Histogram (`bins=`) |
| `geom_boxplot()` | Box plot |
| `geom_bar()` | Bar plot |
| `coord_polar()` | Pie chart (with `geom_bar`) |

### Faceting (Split by Category)
```r
+ facet_wrap(~ var, nrow=2)        # Split by one variable
+ facet_grid(var1 ~ var2)          # Split by two variables
```

---

## dplyr (Data Manipulation)

```r
library(dplyr)
```

| Function | Usage | Note |
|----------|-------|------|
| `filter()` | `filter(df, col == val, col2 > 30)` | Removes NA automatically |
| `arrange()` | `arrange(df, col, desc(col2))` | Sort rows |
| `select()` | `select(df, col1, col2)` | Select columns |
| `mutate()` | `mutate(df, new_col = col1 * 2)` | Add/compute columns |
| `summarise()` | `summarise(df, mean = mean(col))` | Aggregate stats |
| `group_by()` | `group_by(df, col)` | Group before summarise |

### Pipe Operator
```r
df %>% filter(...) %>% select(...) %>% summarise(...)
```

---

## Building R Packages

1. Clean environment: `rm(list = ls())`
2. Load functions to include
3. Create skeleton: `package.skeleton(name='myPackage')`
4. Edit documentation in `./myPackage/man/`
5. Build: `R CMD build myPackage` (in terminal)
6. Install locally: `install.packages("myPackage_1.0.tar.gz", repos=NULL)`
7. Share via CRAN: https://xmpalantir.wu.ac.at/cransubmit/

## Rmarkdown Reporting

### Output Options
```yaml
output:
  html_document: default
  pdf_document: default   # Requires LaTeX
  word_document: default
```

### Text Formatting
- `#`, `##`, `###` - Sections
- `*italic*`, `**bold**`
- `>` - Quote/comment box
- `[text](url)` - Links

### Code Chunk Options
| Option | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| `eval=FALSE` | Show code, don't run |
| `echo=FALSE` | Run code, hide source |
| `include=FALSE` | Run code, hide everything |
| `` `r expression` `` | Inline R result |

### Multi-language Support
````
```{python}
x = 2.5
print(x)
```
````

## Shiny Apps

### Structure
Two files in same directory:
- `ui.R` - User interface
- `server.R` - Server logic

### ui.R Template
```r
library(shiny)
library(bslib)

ui <- page_sidebar(
  title = "App Title",
  sidebar = sidebar(
    sliderInput(inputId = "bins", label = "Bins:", min = 1, max = 50, value = 30),
    checkboxInput(inputId = "density", label = "Show density"),
    selectInput(inputId = "color", label = "Color", choices = c("red","green","blue")),
    numericInput(inputId = "width", label = "Width", value = 2, min = 0.5, max = 5, step = 0.5)
  ),
  plotOutput(outputId = "distPlot")
)
```

### server.R Template
```r
server <- function(input, output) {
  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
    # Access inputs via input$bins, input$density, etc.
    if (input$density) {
      hist(data, breaks = input$bins, freq = FALSE)
      lines(density(data), col = input$color, lwd = input$width)
    } else {
      hist(data, breaks = input$bins)
    }
  })
}
```

### Input Widgets
| Widget | Function |
|--------|----------|
| Slider | `sliderInput()` |
| Checkbox | `checkboxInput()` |
| Dropdown | `selectInput()` |
| Number | `numericInput()` |
| Text | `textInput()` |

### Output Types
| Output | Render Function |
|--------|-----------------|
| `plotOutput()` | `renderPlot({})` |
| `tableOutput()` | `renderTable({})` |
| `textOutput()` | `renderText({})` |

### Run App
```r
shiny::runApp("path/to/app/directory")
```

## Key Takeaways

- **R is vectorized** - operations apply to whole vectors
- **Indexing starts at 1** (not 0 like Python)
- **Use `<-` for assignment** inside function calls
- **Data frames** = tables with mixed column types
- **Lists** = most flexible structure, functions return lists

- **Functions**: `name <- function(params) { return(result) }`
- **Loops**: `for`, `while` - avoid when vectorized alternative exists
- **`...`** passes extra args to subfunctions (great for plot customization)

- **ggplot2**: Grammar of graphics, layer-based (`+`)
- **Faceting**: Split plots by category with `facet_wrap`/`facet_grid`
- **Rmarkdown**: Mix text + code, export to HTML/PDF/Word
- **Packages**: `package.skeleton()` → edit docs → `R CMD build`

- **dplyr** for large data: `filter`, `select`, `mutate`, `summarise`, `arrange`
- **`filter()` removes NA** automatically (unlike base R)
- **Pipe `%>%`**: Chain operations without intermediate variables
- **`group_by()` + `summarise()`** = powerful aggregation

### Golden Rules
1. **Vectorize** - avoid loops when possible
2. **Check for NA** - use `na.rm=TRUE` or handle explicitly
3. **Use packages** - don't reinvent the wheel (dplyr, ggplot2)
4. **Document** - Rmarkdown for reproducible reports
